LESSON: GUIDED READING: FLUENCY

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Reading 2.1 Reading Aloud: Arabic Alphabet (2 sessions) • Arabic Alphabetic Char
Topic 2.6: Guided Reading: Fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided Reading: Fluency, part of Reading 2.1 Reading Aloud: Arabic Alphabet (2 sessions) • Arabic Alphabetic Char in Grade 4 ARABIC LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to read words with correct pronunciation?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. team up to list vocabulary related to the theme from a short passage,

2. read words related to household items aloud using correct pronunciation,

3. peer assess each other’s reading for fluency in terms of pronunciation,

4. team up to conduct a spelling bee contest to spell simple words related to the theme.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. team up to list vocabulary related to the theme from a short passage,
2. read words related to household items aloud using correct pronunciation,
3. peer assess each other’s reading for fluency in terms of pronunciation,
4. team up to conduct a spelling bee contest to spell simple words related to the theme.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided Reading: Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: This is developed as learner keenly articulates sounds in simple words related to the

theme.

26

• Citizenship: This is promoted as the learner embraces each other’s role when teaming up to conduct a spelling bee contest to

spell simple words related to the theme.

Values:
Integrity: This is enhanced as the learner gives honest and constructive feedback to peers while peer assessing each other’s

reading for fluency in terms of pronunciation.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental awareness: This is addressed as the learner recognises household items and describes their location in relation to

others.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner is able to relate the concept of household items to similar concepts as covered in Agriculture.
